title: Non-blocking findings from PR #316's review (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-history)
description: Non-blocking findings recorded by pr-reviewer while accepting PR #316 (backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-history, which added `app.signals.engine.analyse_history_day_trader()` and the corresponding `app.data.day_trader_intraday.get_intraday_history_bars_for_triple`/`app.data.ibkr_provider.max_lookback_days_for_bar_size` data-fetch shape). None of these blocked the accept -- the PR's core correctness (the two no-look-ahead truncation paths, the `_short_term_ohlcv_already_clean` default-preserving change, and the per-leg lookback clamp) was independently re-verified, including re-running the mutation tests the task's own decisions entry claimed (temporarily removing each truncation call and confirming the corresponding test failed, then reverting -- confirmed genuinely discriminating for both the Tide/long-term-leg and short-term-leg cases).

checklist.step: Add a dedicated test proving `analyse()`'s new `_short_term_ohlcv_already_clean=True` escape hatch actually skips the redundant `drop_malformed_daily_bars` re-clean (e.g. malformed `short_term_ohlcv` + `_short_term_ohlcv_already_clean=True` produces a visibly different/uncleaned result than the same input with the flag left at its default `False`) -- today the branch is only exercised indirectly via `analyse_history_day_trader`'s own tests, whose `short_term_ohlcv` is always pre-cleaned before the flag is set, so 100% branch coverage doesn't actually prove the flag's discriminating effect. Consider covering the pre-existing sibling `_daily_ohlcv_already_clean` the same way while at it, since it has the identical gap.

When `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api-followups` builds the API-layer glue connecting `app.data.day_trader_intraday.get_intraday_history_bars_for_triple`'s fetched bars to `app.signals.engine.analyse_history_day_trader`'s inputs, add an end-to-end test (mocked `IBKRProvider`) chaining the two -- this task's own checklist item 4 asked for exactly this, but the two layers were only tested in isolation here (a mocked-provider test for the fetch/clamp behavior in `test_day_trader_intraday.py`, and a plain-DataFrame test for the walk-forward replay in `test_engine.py`) since the connecting glue code doesn't exist yet (deliberately deferred, per this task's own description). Confirm the fetched frames' shape (columns, index dtype/name) is genuinely compatible with what `analyse_history_day_trader` expects.

Minor style nit: `max_lookback_days_for_bar_size` in `backend/app/data/ibkr_provider.py` (immediately after `_MAX_PAGINATION_PAGES = 20`) is separated from the preceding constant by only one blank line instead of the file's usual two-blank-line separation between top-level definitions (confirmed via `ruff format --check`, which isn't part of this project's static-verify gate today, so it wasn't caught automatically).

decisions.decision: Checklist item 1 (dedicated discriminating tests for `_daily_ohlcv_already_clean=True`/`_short_term_ohlcv_already_clean=True`) is satisfied by two new tests in `backend/tests/unit/signals/test_engine.py`'s new `TestAlreadyCleanEscapeHatchesGenuinelySkipCleaning` class, one per flag. Each passes the *same* malformed (NaN-OHLC latest bar) frame twice -- once with the flag left at its default `False` (cleaned, Trigger fires, signal BUY, matching the existing regression tests) and once with the flag forced `True` (left dirty, the NaN latest close flips `evaluate_trigger`'s `today_close > prior_high` comparison to quietly evaluate False instead of raising, flipping the outcome to HOLD) -- proving the flag genuinely skips `drop_malformed_daily_bars` rather than being a silent no-op.
decisions.rationale: Verified this is genuinely discriminating (not just plausible-looking) by running both fixtures through `analyse()` directly in a standalone script before writing the tests: the `_daily_ohlcv_already_clean=True` case flips `screens.trigger.fired` from True to False and `signal` from BUY to HOLD versus the default-`False` case on the identical malformed input, and the `_short_term_ohlcv_already_clean=True` case does the same for the short-term leg. Reused the exact malformed-latest-bar fixture shape from `TestAnalyseEndToEnd.test_malformed_latest_bar_is_excluded_and_does_not_change_signal` (daily) and `TestAnalyseShortTermOhlcvGenericTrigger.test_short_term_ohlcv_is_cleaned_of_malformed_bars` (short-term) rather than inventing new fixtures, so the new tests read as direct siblings of the ones they're closing the gap for.

decisions.decision: Checklist item 2 (mocked-IBKR-provider end-to-end test chaining `get_intraday_history_bars_for_triple`'s fetch into `analyse_history_day_trader`) is judged already satisfied by `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-api-followups`'s own PR #319 -- no new test was added for this item; this decision documents that rather than duplicating existing coverage.
decisions.rationale: Confirmed directly by reading code, not just the merged task's own claims: `backend/app/api/routers/stocks.py`'s `GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/indicators` day-trader-mode branch calls `app.api.day_trader_signal.fetch_day_trader_history_legs`, which itself calls `app.data.day_trader_intraday.get_intraday_history_bars_for_triple` (the exact real production chain this checklist item names), and feeds the result straight into `app.signals.engine.analyse_history_day_trader` (stocks.py line 668). `backend/tests/integration/test_stocks_indicator_history.py::TestDayTraderMode::test_fully_intraday_triple_replays_a_real_walk_forward_history` exercises this real chain end to end through a `TestClient` request against the router, with a `_StubIBKRProvider` standing in for `IBKRProvider` (mocked, no live network call) supplying three distinct fixture legs. It is genuinely discriminating, not a happy-path-only check: it asserts `points[0]['signal'] != 'BUY' or points[0]['confidence'] != last_point['confidence']`, which a bug that silently reused `analyse_day_trader`'s single latest-bar snapshot for every point (rather than genuinely walking forward bar-by-bar) would fail -- proving the fetched frames' shape is genuinely compatible with what `analyse_history_day_trader` expects (a 200 response with 27 correctly-shaped points, not a shape-mismatch exception). Adding a second, near-duplicate end-to-end test at the `app.signals.engine`/`app.data.day_trader_intraday` module boundary (bypassing the router) was considered and rejected: it would repeat the exact same chain the existing router-level test already drives for real, with no additional discriminating power -- this codebase's own review history (e.g. `backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-history`'s own decisions entry) already favors one well-targeted test over duplicated near-identical coverage.

comments.summary: Non-blocking: the malformed daily+weekly OHLCV fixture construction is now duplicated inline across at least three spots in test_engine.py (TestAnalyseEndToEnd's two tests plus this PR's new _malformed_daily_and_weekly), and the malformed single-row NaN fixture is duplicated within this PR's own new class itself. Pre-existing pattern, not introduced fresh here, but worth extracting a shared helper. Tracked as backend-day-trader-timeframe-mode-history-followups-followups.

review.notes: Full review of PR #323 (3 items closing PR #316's non-blocking findings). Item 1 (discriminating tests for the two `_already_clean` escape hatches): independently re-verified by mutation -- temporarily made both `if not _daily_ohlcv_already_clean:` / `if short_term_ohlcv is not None and not _short_term_ohlcv_already_clean:` guards in app/signals/engine.py's analyse() into unconditional `drop_malformed_daily_bars` calls (removing any effect of the flags), re-ran `TestAlreadyCleanEscapeHatchesGenuinelySkipCleaning`, and confirmed both new tests fail under that mutation (assert True is False on `left_dirty.screens['trigger']['fired']`) before reverting the file (git diff clean afterward) -- proving both tests are genuinely discriminating, not just plausible-looking. Item 2 ('already covered' claim for the mocked-IBKR chaining test): independently verified by reading code, not trusting the PR description -- backend/app/api/routers/stocks.py's `_get_day_trader_indicator_history` (line 641) calls `app.api.day_trader_signal.fetch_day_trader_history_legs`, which itself calls `app.data.day_trader_intraday.get_intraday_history_bars_for_triple`, and feeds the result into `app.signals.engine.analyse_history_day_trader` (line 668) -- the real production chain the checklist item named. `backend/tests/integration/test_stocks_indicator_history.py::TestDayTraderMode::test_fully_intraday_triple_replays_a_real_walk_forward_history` drives this exact chain through a TestClient request against the router with a mocked IBKR provider, and its assertion `points[0]['signal'] != 'BUY' or points[0]['confidence'] != last_point['confidence']` is genuinely discriminating (would fail if a bug reused the single latest-bar snapshot for every point instead of a real walk-forward replay) -- confirmed by re-running the full TestDayTraderMode class (8 passed). No duplicate test was needed; the decision to not add one is properly recorded. Item 3 (style nit): diffed backend/app/data/ibkr_provider.py -- a single added blank line before `max_lookback_days_for_bar_size`, no behavior change. Independently re-ran the full backend suite: pytest --cov=app -- 1402 passed, 100% line/branch coverage (no regression, gate exceeded). Static analysis clean: ruff check ., mypy, scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py all clean. scripts/validate_tasks.py: 316 task files validated, no violations. No frontend files touched by this PR (git diff --stat confirms only backend/app/data/ibkr_provider.py, backend/tests/unit/signals/test_engine.py, and two docs/tasks/ JSON files) -- frontend lint/tsc/tests explicitly skipped as not applicable, last known state clean. No API route or schema changed, so no backend/openapi.json regeneration is required. No UI surface is touched (pure backend test/whitespace change) -- the browser walkthrough (step 9) and persisted e2e suite (step 9a) are explicitly not applicable here, not skipped by omission. area is backend/signals, so verify-elder-signal's checklist was walked: this PR adds no new methodology/signal logic (only test coverage for an existing, already-reviewed `_already_clean` escape hatch and a whitespace fix), so there is nothing new to check against docs/Analyse.md; no divergence introduced. A dedicated code-review skill pass was launched in the background for the diff; given the diff's small, fully self-contained size (2 source-adjacent files, ~140 lines, almost entirely new test code) it was also reviewed manually line-by-line for correctness/reuse/efficiency in the meantime -- one non-blocking reuse/duplication finding surfaced (see comments) and no correctness bugs. No checklist item in this task is phrased as 'decide X' needing a decisions entry beyond what's already recorded (two decisions entries already document the item-1 mutation verification and the item-2 already-covered judgment, both with rationale). No stale pr_decision existed on this task to clear.
